meta.title: Use your framework's devtools from the toolbar today

security.label: Step with an evidenced pain point

nodes.label: App mounts devtools
nodes.explanation: The journey starts on any app page devhost serves with its toolbar injected and [devtools.externalToolbars].enabled = true, the default. The app mounts its own devtools: TanStack Router, Query or the unified TanStack shell (Form, Table and Pacer plugins), React Hook Form DevTool, Jotai DevTools, or Vue DevTools in a Vite DevTools dock. Redux Toolkit and Zustand stores are registered through /__devhost__/redux.js instead, because the Redux inspector is devhost's own and has no native launcher. One combined detector reads every integration's adapters.

sources.label: One detector combines every integration
Redux: register stores through redux.js

nodes.label: Detect + hide launchers
nodes.sublabel: in the page, once per frame
nodes.explanation: A MutationObserver on the page body, plus the Vue and Redux subscriptions, schedules one resync per animation frame. Every installed adapter becomes a toolbar entry with its label, hover title and open state, and one stylesheet hides the native launchers with display: none !important. Vue's dock launcher is hidden with a stylesheet adopted inside the dock's shadow root, and only while the dock is trusted, visible and has one Vue entry. Entries appear and disappear as libraries mount and unmount, with no page reload.

sources.label: Observe the page; rebuild entries per frame
Hide native launchers with display: none

nodes.label: Find the launcher
nodes.explanation: The toolbar gains one unlabeled segment of identical monospace text buttons between the resource readouts and Hold Reloads, for example Router, Query, TanStack, Form 1, Jotai 1 and Redux, with no icons or grouping. Form 1 is React Hook Form's inspector, while the page's TanStack Form instance sits under TanStack, so Form names neither library; the library appears only in hover text ('Toggle React Hook Form inspector 1'). Jotai 1 is numbered although the page has one Jotai panel, because the detector always appends its discovery number; numbers follow discovery order and restart on reload, as documented (third-party-devtools-06).

sources.label: Text buttons; library named only in title
React Hook Form entry labelled Form N
Jotai N even with one store

nodes.label: Click the native control
nodes.explanation: Choosing an entry runs toggleLauncher: it asks that entry's adapter whether its panel is open, clicks the library's own close control when it is and its open control otherwise, then re-reads every entry each frame for up to 60 frames until the pressed state matches. Nothing devhost draws opens: the library's own panel does, or for Redux devhost's monitor popup. The toggle never considers other open panels or a monitor window hidden behind the app. A press can also change nothing and say nothing: open() and close() return nothing, each adapter that clicks the page's markup does nothing when its selector misses, and a watch whose state never changed ends on the same exit as success, with no notice, no new tooltip and no console line. Detection is looser than the actions (Router and Query count as installed from their panel alone), so a library release that moves a control leaves a dead entry; a moved React Hook Form launcher even makes a closed inspector read pressed while devhost keeps hiding that launcher (third-party-devtools-07).

sources.label: Toggle: close when open, else open
Watch 60 frames; no change ends silently
Router clicks only a control it finds

nodes.label: Panel docks at bottom
nodes.explanation: Router, Query, the unified TanStack shell and Jotai dock to the bottom edge at fixed heights (Router and Query 500 px, TanStack 400 px, Jotai 372 px); React Hook Form opens a full-height right column. The entry reads pressed, and choosing it again closes the panel. devhost's toolbar stays fixed in the bottom-right corner above every docked panel: at 1280x800 it covers x 213-1260 of the panel's bottom 30 px, so a list's last row stays hidden even when scrolled to the end, and at 900 px the wrapped toolbar covers more. That slice of third-party-devtools-01 belongs to the toolbar-shell redesign; devhost never moves library panels by design.

sources.label: Toolbar fixed bottom-right in the dock layer
Launchers only; panels are never reparented

nodes.label: Open a second panel
nodes.explanation: A second panel that docks to the same edge lands exactly on top of the first: at 1280x800 Router and then Query both sit at 0,299 1280x501 with Query painted over Router, and both entries read pressed while only Query is visible. While Query is open, Router cannot be reached: choosing Router closes it underneath Query, choosing it again reopens it underneath, and neither click changes anything on screen except Router's own button. The docs accept the overlap ('close one from the toolbar to reach another', integrations/jotai.md), but the pressed state cannot say which panel is visible (third-party-devtools-01).

sources.label: Router reads open while covered
Docs: open panels can overlap

nodes.label: Close the top panel
nodes.explanation: To reach the panel underneath, people close the top one. Router keeps its close chevron, React Hook Form its X and Jotai its minimize button, but devhost's hide stylesheet also removes TanStack Query's minimize button and the TanStack shell's 'Close TanStack Devtools' button. Query still closes from its 'TANSTACK React Query v5' logo, a button that looks like a logo; the shell closes with Escape, which does nothing for Query. With the toolbar collapsed to its dot, an open Query panel closes only through that logo. integrations/tanstack.md says devhost hides 'their floating launcher buttons' and that 'its own close buttons keep the toolbar's pressed state in step' (third-party-devtools-02).

sources.label: Query: minimize button hidden too
Shell: its close button hidden
Docs: own close buttons stay in step

nodes.label: Redux monitor opens
nodes.explanation: Choosing Redux opens devhost's own monitor as a separate 1000x760 popup window under a new session ID; the popup connects back over a MessageChannel and starts every registered store. The store picker opens on the placeholder 'Select...' although stores are registered, and with nothing chosen the action list follows whichever store changed last: after Redux count and then Zustand count only zustand/setState shows, while the picker still reads 'Select...'. Every monitor window is titled 'Redux DevTools', a constant in the page devhost serves, so two projects' monitors cannot be told apart in the window switcher (third-party-devtools-04).

sources.label: New session; 1000x760 popup
Monitor store starts with no store chosen
Every monitor titled Redux DevTools

nodes.label: Monitor behind the app
nodes.explanation: Clicking back into the app puts the popup behind the app window. The Redux entry still reads pressed, titled 'Close Redux DevTools: connected to 2 registered host stores', and clicking it, the obvious way to get the window back, closes the monitor: the toggle calls close() whenever the window is open, so the session's focus() branch is never reached and nothing in devhost shows a hidden monitor. Choosing Redux again opens a new window with the picker back on 'Select...'; Redux Toolkit history survives in the app's store, but Zustand history restarts at a new @@INIT. Reloading the app page also closes the monitor; both restarts are documented limitations (third-party-devtools-03).

sources.label: Pressed entry always calls close()
focus() only reached through open()
Page reload (pagehide) closes the monitor

nodes.label: A store cannot connect
nodes.explanation: A store devhost cannot inspect, such as a Redux store registered without instrument(), leaves the Redux entry looking exactly like a working one, with the same classes and colors. The only sign is its hover text, 'Redux DevTools unavailable: Cart store: Redux DevTools requires the public instrument EnhancedStore.liftedStore capability...', which says unavailable even while the other stores connect; after opening, the monitor repeats that sentence as a banner with no link to the setup steps. A popup the browser blocks is just as silent: nothing opens, the entry stays unpressed, and its only message, the hover text 'Allow popups for this project and try again.', is masked by any store's setup error. integrations/redux.md describes exactly this tooltip, so the design, not the docs, is the problem (third-party-devtools-04).

sources.label: Registration errors kept per store
First error becomes the hover title
Entry shows only title and pressed state

nodes.label: Set enabled = false
nodes.explanation: The only opt-out is one manifest key, [devtools.externalToolbars].enabled; the manifest accepts no other key in that table. The example manifest describes false as 'leave third-party launcher buttons untouched', guides/devtools.md as 'leave their launchers alone', and each integration page presents it as that integration's own opt-out. The edit applies by hot reload: devhost sends the new configuration on the health stream and the page swaps it in without a reload.

sources.label: One key for every integration
Example: false leaves launchers untouched
Health stream swaps the config live

nodes.label: Every entry disappears
nodes.explanation: With enabled = false the toolbar clears every entry and removes the hide stylesheet: native launchers come back and open panels stay as they are, as documented. Redux goes too, and the Redux inspector has no native launcher, so registered Redux and Zustand stores can no longer be inspected at all and an open monitor closes. A team that prefers one library's own launcher must give up every integration (third-party-devtools-05). The restored TanStack launchers then sit half under devhost's toolbar in the bottom-right corner, which toolbar-shell-02 covers.

sources.label: Off: clear every entry, drop the style
Redux is one adapter of the same switch

cards.title: What already works
items: Native launchers stop covering the page: one toolbar segment proxies open and close through each library's own controls, and the panels stay the libraries' own
Pressed state follows the panels: a DOM observer keeps entries in step when a panel closes from its own control, Escape or a hotkey
Entries appear and vanish as libraries mount and unmount, with no page reload; Vue is offered only from a trusted dock with one Vue entry
The Redux monitor needs no browser extension; closing its window unpresses the entry within 100 ms, and Redux Toolkit history survives a reopen
The opt-out applies by hot reload without a page reload and leaves open panels as they are

cards.title: Tickets on this journey
items: third-party-devtools-01 A second panel docked to the same edge buries the first while both entries read pressed (the toolbar covering every docked panel's last row is the toolbar-shell slice)
third-party-devtools-03 Clicking the pressed Redux entry to find the monitor closes it; reopening or reloading restarts Zustand history
third-party-devtools-04 The Redux monitor never names the store shown or the project, and a store that cannot connect shows only in hover text
third-party-devtools-05 Opting out is all or nothing and also removes the Redux inspector, which has no native launcher
third-party-devtools-02 devhost hides the Query and TanStack panels' own close buttons, unlike the other three panels, while the docs say it hides only launchers
third-party-devtools-06 Launchers are look-alike text buttons: Form 1 is React Hook Form, and the library is named only in hover text
third-party-devtools-07 A launcher whose library control devhost cannot find, as after a devtools update, does nothing and says nothing
toolbar-shell-02 Owned by toolbar-shell: native launchers restored by the opt-out sit half under devhost's toolbar

cards.title: Evidence
items: Traced from alexgorbatchev/devhost at edb5c0fc01cabae490e92ac23d4c785ec896c4ed; the review exercised build 0.0.12 live on a page mounting TanStack Router, Query and the unified shell, React Hook Form, Jotai, Redux Toolkit and Zustand: opening, stacking and closing panels, the Redux popup (a tab in headless Chrome), a store without instrument(), and the opt-out by hot reload. Vue DevTools and TanStack Detach were not exercised (no Vue app; no picture-in-picture in headless Chrome). This diagram was traced from source only; third-party-devtools-07 was verified from code only, since the review ran only tested library versions.
